title: The Shaking Restaurant
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, and the police officers Megure/Takagi/Chiba who appear only in routine investigative capacities) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved. The episode actually layers TWO plots: (1) Reiko Hanaoka and cook Minoru Wada, having an affair that Shigeru Hanaoka had begun investigating via a private detective, rig an elaborate delayed-fall trap using a frozen replica of the restaurant's display vase, a fishing line, and a metal bar at the adjacent construction site, intending it to look like an accident caused by the construction shaking; (2) waitress Saki Yoshizawa -- secretly Hanaoka's daughter by Aiko Morimura, a woman he abandoned pregnant on Hachijou Island 21 years earlier -- independently kills him with a frozen sea bream shortly before the vase trap ever triggers, then rushes off to establish an alibi with Ran/Conan at a video shop. The vase falls hours later on an already-dead body, which is what exposes Reiko/Wada's scheme as a separate, failed murder attempt rather than the actual cause of death; fish-scale residue in the head wound (matching the sea bream, not the ceramic vase) is the pivotal clue separating the two plots. The old wiki-summary case file got the culprit right (Saki/s2) but flattened Reiko and Wada's scheme into 'an unrelated staged prank others had planned' -- it was in fact its own attempted-murder plot with a real motive (the affair, and Hanaoka's PI investigation of it) -- and omitted Aiko Morimura and Yamamoto entirely, plus collapsed all evidence into one generic clue/knows edges instead of the several independently-informative physical clues the transcript actually supports.

clues.desc: A scratch mark on the ceiling beam above the stairs matches a second scratch on the window frame facing the construction site -- showing the same taut line ran from the beam, through the vase, out the window, to the site.

The flowers scattered from the fallen vase were still fresh, inconsistent with the vase having fallen hours earlier during the pre-10:30pm construction shaking -- proving the fall was deliberately delayed and timed rather than a genuine accident.

The autopsy placed Hanaoka's time of death between 11pm and 1am, but the construction crew's shaking-causing drilling had already stopped at 10:30pm due to a machine malfunction -- proving the vase could not have fallen on its own from the shaking and the 'accident' was staged.

Fish scales matching the frozen sea bream, not ceramic vase fragments, were found embedded in the wound on Hanaoka's head and neck -- proving the fatal blow was struck by the sea bream and that the vase (found broken beside him) fell on a body already dead.
